transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-22 15:00 PDT
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Recording id: ff-20260422-nq-01
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood SE), Marcus (NovaQuant VP Eng), Jordan (CTO), Priya (ML Lead), Leah (SRE)

Summary:
High-level POC scoping for NovaQuant pilot focusing on quality evaluation and workload sizing. Main goals: define success criteria (accuracy/format/hallucination tolerances), identify golden prompts and regression tests, establish benchmark matrix (latency, cost, golden-set pass rates), agree pilot timeline and next steps. Security and data residency briefly mentioned; customer requires audit logs and KMS support.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria and acceptance gates
- Workload sizing and expected qps
- Benchmarks and test harness
- Golden prompts and regression suite design
- Hallucination detection and format checks
- Scoring approach and pass/fail thresholds
- Timeline and pilot logistics

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect at times):
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Marcus: Marcus here. vp eng at NovaQuant. we're trying to accelerate model-assisted research summaries and parameter explainers, so low hallucination is a must.
[00:18] Jordan: Jordan, cto. watching infra and cost tradeoffs closely.
[00:22] Priya: Priya, leading ML. i’ll own the golden prompts and evals.
[00:26] Leah: Leah, SRE — i'll validate load and tail latency requirements.
[00:30] Samira: Samira from Redwood, se - i'll run the benchmark harness and help with KV cache / batching config.
[00:36] Evan: Evan here, solutions eng, can help with instrumentation and telemetry.
[00:40] Alex: goal today — agree success criteria, what to test, and a pilot timeline.
[00:48] Marcus: our immediate risk is hallucination introducing incorrect trading signals — we need deterministic guard rails.
[00:55] Samira: understood. for NovaQuant we usually recommend a golden-set + regression playlist approach plus format checks to make sure outputs follow the regulatory template.
[01:05] Priya: what do you mean by format checks? can you give example?
[01:09] Samira: yeah so for you, the model must return a JSON blob with fields: summary, confidence_score, citations[] where citations are either pass-through id references to original docs or null. the format check asserts schema compliance and fails the sample if parsing errors occur.
[01:25] Jordan: we also want a hallucination metric: percent of claims that are not supported by source docs. how do you measure that at scale?
[01:33] Evan: we run an automated entailment/back-check step. golden prompts with annotated references let us measure unsupported claims. it’s noisy so we use human-in-the-loop sampling for borderline cases.
[01:45] Marcus: timeline — we want to run a one month pilot with 2 weeks of benchmarks and 2 weeks of production-ish traffic. is that realistic?
[01:53] Alex: yes, typical is 4–6 weeks. week 0 is onboarding and ingest, week 1 run baselines & golden set, week 2 run load + tuning, week 3 wrap with regression and acceptance. makes sense?
[02:05] Priya: sounds good. question on workload sizing: our daily active analysts are about 80, peak concurrent requests ~40 at minute bursts, avg req size 350 tokens, 80% requests are short summaries, 20% are multi-doc explainers.
[02:20] Leah: tail latency target 95th < 450ms for short summaries, we could tolerate 1.2s for multi-docs.
[02:29] Samira: great, we'll provision test harness to simulate 50 qps with bursts to 120 qps to stress autoscaling and batching. we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[02:42] Marcus: cost per 1k tokens — show us the delta between hosted and dedicated capacity.
[02:47] Alex: sure, i'll include three pricing rows: hosted on-demand, dedicated reserved small pool, dedicated with burst credits.
[02:54] Jordan: about data — can the KV cache be flushed per-tenant, and we need the option for no cross-tenant caching?
[02:59] Samira: yes, we support tenant-isolated KV cache and prefix-keying; we can also show a demo of per-request cache controls.
[03:08] Priya: on golden prompts — we'll provide 50 high-importance prompts that represent our worst-case queries (long context, many entities). we expect at least 90% pass on format + no hallucination for the golden set.
[03:21] Samira: 90% is a good starting gate. for hallucination we usually set a 98% citation-precision target for the golden set, but that's strict; is there any regulatory target?
[03:31] Marcus: not a hard number, but 98% seems high. maybe 95% citation precision acceptable for initial pilot if we can triage errors quickly.
[03:39] Alex: note that citation-precision measures fraction of asserted facts that match source references; we'll run automatic checks, then sample for human review at 5% sampling.
[03:49] Jordan: how do you handle hallucination detection on novel facts like derived inferences?
[03:53] Evan: we mark those as 'inference' and flag low confidence. heuristics include overlap with source spans, entailment model score, and presence of explicit citation tokens. we return a confidence band in the JSON to help downstream gating.
[04:07] Priya: regression tests — want to run nightly regression on golden-set and a smaller smoke every deploy. how long does nightly take?
[04:13] Samira: depends on tokens and model. with our harness, 50 golden prompts with full context runs in ~25 minutes against a single model variant; parallelizing across variants shortens it. we'll provide runtime estimates in the benchmark sheet.
[04:26] Leah: we need audit logs and SSO. SAML + SCIM is mandatory for enterprise SSO. also KMS for key wrap.
[04:33] Alex: Redwood supports SAML and SCIM; private deployments can integrate customer KMS/HSM. i'll include SOC2 and ISO summary and a link to the security pack.
[04:44] Jordan: do you store logs with PII stripped? we need redact before retention.
[04:48] Samira: logs by default can be configured to strip PII, and retention windows are configurable; for dedicated we can do no retention for request payloads.
[04:57] Marcus: benchmark metrics — we want: p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, hallucination rate (automated + human-sampled), format compliance rate, throughput under sustained load, and recovery time after overload.
[05:11] Evan: we’ll add model-switch failover timings and fallback to cheaper variant metric.
[05:16] Priya: scoring approach — do you have a rubric?
[05:19] Samira: yes. we propose a weighted scoring: 40% golden-set pass rate (format+citation), 25% hallucination automated metric (lower is better), 15% latency SLO attainment, 10% cost per 1k tokens relative to baseline, 10% operational (logs/SSO/KMS integration completeness). pass threshold 75% weighted score and no critical regressions in golden-set.
[05:40] Jordan: that helps. can we tweak weights? ML team will propose 2 variants of scoring and you can test both in the eval.
[05:48] Alex: good — we'll run both scoring rubrics and show side-by-side.
[05:52] Marcus: on benchmarks, we want to compare two model families: open Llama-like quantized 4-bit variant vs a larger 8-bit family. can you show token-cost delta?
[06:02] Samira: yes example workloads will give cost per 1k tokens and latency curves. we'll also show quantization impact on hallucination patterns — sometimes aggressive quantization increases hallucination in rare tokens.
[06:15] Priya: for regression tests, we want deterministic seeds and a stable tokenizer to avoid flakiness.
[06:21] Evan: we'll pin model versions for the test harness and capture RNG seeds; plus rerun failed cases with higher sampling to confirm.
[06:30] Leah: runbook — if latency exceeds SLO during pilot, we'd like automatic fallback to cheaper variant and an alert to our SRE channel.
[06:38] Samira: Redwood supports canary and automatic fallback policies; we'll show a sample runbook and alerting integration (PagerDuty webhook example).
[06:46] Marcus: what's the acceptance gating at end of pilot?
[06:49] Alex: formal acceptance: weighted score >= 75% and zero critical hallucinations in the golden 50, and integration checklist complete (SSO, logs, KMS or data residency).
[06:58] Priya: critical hallucination defined as an assertion that contradicts source documents or invents nonexistent citations?
[07:02] Samira: correct — those are immediate fails for the sample.
[07:06] Jordan: anything about private deployment? we might want a VPC/private control plane later. can you outline options?
[07:12] Alex: yes, options: hosted (fastest), dedicated reserved capacity (predictable latency), private (VPC + customer-managed control plane) — we'll include pros/cons and expected onboarding times in the SOW.
[07:23] Marcus: final check — action items?
[07:26] Alex: recap, we'll share: pilot SOW & pricing, benchmark spreadsheet link, security pack, and a short tech-deep-dive calendar invite.
[07:36] Priya: we’ll send golden prompts and some labeled citations.
[07:40] Leah: i'll send tail-latency dashboards and infra notes.
[07:44] Marcus: thanks all — let's aim to start 2026-05-11 if contract signed.
[07:48] Alex: thanks everyone. end.

Notes / Artifacts referenced:
- benchmark-spreadsheet.csv (link shared in chat)
- Redwood security-pack.pdf (provided via SSO link)
- sample runbook and alerting webhooks (PagerDuty example)

Quality and evaluation specifics (from call, condensed):
- Golden prompts: NovaQuant to supply 50 critical prompts (Priya). Redwood to run golden-set against all candidate model variants. Golden-set scoring includes format compliance, citation-precision, hallucination flagging.
- Regression tests: nightly full golden-set run; smoke tests on deploys. Deterministic seeds, pinned model versions.
- Hallucination/format checks: automated entailment/back-check, schema validation, confidence bands. Human-in-loop review on sampled failures (5% sampling).
- Scoring approach: weighted rubric (40% golden pass, 25% hallucination, 15% latency SLO, 10% cost, 10% ops). Pass threshold 75% and zero critical hallucination in golden set.
- Workload sizing and benchmarks: simulate 50 qps sustained with 120 qps bursts, capture p50/p95/p99, throughput, and fallbacks. Acceptable latency p95: 450ms short, 1.2s multi-doc.

End of transcript.
